page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-8GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server configured with 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It runs on the KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The underlying processor is an AMD EPYC 7542 with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and a shared CPU allocation model. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of average and weak performance characteristics, reflecting its shared resource model. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is poor, falling into the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance is weak at the bottom 25%. However, Geekbench scores present an average profile, with a single-core score of 1484.0 and a multi-core score of 5232.0. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 398.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 40.7 GB/sec for large blocks, but large block write bandwidth is weak at 23.27 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform moderately, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 24.4 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which limits sustained multi-threaded performance and leads to weaker results in resource-intensive tasks like software compilation and Redis SET operations. Qualitatively, the instance offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources, providing a cost-efficient option for lightweight applications. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments that can tolerate shared CPU performance.

Performance benchmarks show a split profile: while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores align with average tiers, stress-ng CPU tests and write memory bandwidth fall into the lower percentiles.
